expectations.text: The output includes an Executive Summary
expectations.evidence: The output contains a dedicated `## Executive Summary` section in the Analysis / Deliverable portion.

expectations.text: The output distinguishes IEEE 1012 V&V logic from IEC 61508 / IEC 61511 functional safety lifecycle logic
expectations.evidence: The output has separate sections for IEEE 1012, IEC 61508, and IEC 61511, then states: `IEEE 1012 governs the quality and completeness of V&V activities`, `IEC 61508 governs the generic functional safety lifecycle logic`, and `IEC 61511 adapts that lifecycle into concrete SIS/SIF process-industry practice`.

expectations.text: The output explains that SIL applies to a safety function or SIF rather than simply to a single device
expectations.evidence: The output states: `SIL applies to the safety function or SIF, not simply to one certified component.`

expectations.text: The output includes lifecycle workflow, evidence chain, and engineering recommendations
expectations.evidence: The output contains the sections `## Lifecycle Method`, `## Evidence Chain`, and `## Recommendations`.

expectations.text: The output avoids claiming formal compliance or certification
expectations.evidence: The report frames itself as an engineering positioning report and explicitly states it is not a `formal certification decision`; it also says `No plant-specific evidence set was assessed.`

claims.claim: IEEE 1012, IEC 61508, and IEC 61511 have distinct but complementary roles
claims.evidence: The output explicitly assigns separate roles to V&V process discipline, generic functional safety lifecycle logic, and process-industry SIS/SIF execution.

claims.claim: A device certificate alone is insufficient to justify a SIF SIL claim
claims.evidence: The report directly rejects device-only SIL reasoning and ties SIL to the safety function / SIF.

uncertainties: This was produced through a Codex-native manual execution path rather than an isolated executor agent transcript.
